external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member using the library service to borrow, renew, reserve, borrow or return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login for the circulation page; individual staff members and branches cannot be distinguished in the history.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: Phone application through which members borrow, renew and reserve books and which calls the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books being borrowed or returned, then sends loan and return information to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: What the kiosks communicate with beyond the lending API is unknown.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: REST API that checks loan rules, handles borrowing, renewals, reservations, loans and returns, and is the only stated reader or writer of the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Sources disagree about exposure: Lending service note says "The lending API is internal-only"; Interview transcript says "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." Authentication for phone calls is unverified: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: Database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses and members' full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The earlier statement about two databases was corrected: the databases were merged in the spring, and the old reservations database is gone.

data_flows.name: borrow renew reserve
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew or reserve books.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Member, book, loan and reservation requests.

data_flows.name: renew reserve books
data_flows.description: The library app calls the lending API with member and book or title information to renew loans, borrow books or reserve titles.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: The API authentication mechanism is unknown. Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: Member identity, book or title, and loan or reservation change.

data_flows.name: send loan return
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends each scanned loan and return to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: Member card, book, loan and return information.

data_flows.name: manage loans
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: The circulation page uses one shared desk login; the password is on a card taped under the desk. The history records only that the loan was closed by hand, not which person or branch performed it.
data_flows.data_description: Loan, member account block and return-status changes.

data_flows.name: read write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations and borrowing-history records.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: Network on which the self-service kiosks and desk staff work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: Council data-centre location where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Network over which phones talk directly to the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.
trust_boundaries.notes: This names the network used to reach the API, not the API's placement.

assumptions.assumption: The contents of the loans database are confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: Interview transcript states: "Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database."
